variants: Sold as the Stationary AI kit with frame, accessories, touchscreen and desktop; an optional high-performance Linux workstation bundle is offered alongside. The desk is not included.
availability_note: The product page shows a price of $23,995.95 with BUY NOW and CUSTOM QUOTE controls and states an average production time of 2-3 weeks regardless of shipping rate, with a sales contact for more information.

hardware.compute: A high-performance desktop is included in the kit's four-arm, touchscreen configuration. An optional Linux workstation bundle carries an NVIDIA RTX 5090 and an Intel Core Ultra 9.
hardware.sensors: Four Intel RealSense D405 cameras and a 10-inch touchscreen, in the page's specification row.
hardware.actuation: Two leader-follower pairs of WidowX AI arms, four arms in total, in a bench-mounted frame; the page notes the desk is not included. No joint count is stated on the pages read.

developer_access: Trossen's documentation gives a supported route for running the reader's own policy on the arms. Its OpenPI tutorial walks through using the openpi framework with Trossen AI arms, fine-tuning Pi0 and Pi 0.5 policies on collected data and running inference. The product page claims extensive API and SDK support for customizing workflows with interoperability across PyTorch and TensorFlow, alongside MuJoCo simulation and LeRobot integration.
terms_note: Trossen's Terms & Conditions, last updated July 10, 2026, cover products, purchases and payment, shipping, and a return and refund policy, so they are recorded as terms of sale. The product page lists a 3-year warranty on the workstation bundle. No SDK licence was found at review time.

terms_evidence.scope: Terms & Conditions: products, purchases and payment, shipping, return and refund policy

not_verified: The OpenPI policy route and the kit's capabilities are Trossen Robotics' own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a Trossen Robotics web page or documentation page the company can change at any time.
